summary: This is a sound stage-1 rewrite, aimed at the one place left with real headroom: full-layer decode at batch 16/32, which is 72-81% of those loads and runs at 2.1 TB/s against a 4.8 TB/s floor. load_inline is explicitly allowed. The weakest link is the 3.3 TB/s target on uniformly random 128-byte rows, and stage 1's milestone will measure it directly. Fix three robustness gaps before claiming: when the kernel compiles, a batch<=64 gate, and PAIRED=False on the gated path.
justification: Profile support is strong. At decode_16 the full layer takes 156.8 us (FA3 main 150.4, combine 4.4, prepare 3.0) against a 63.2 us floor. At decode_32 it takes 298.5 us (main 292.0) against 126.4 us. Both are ~2.4x off the floor and these are the largest absolute rows in the problem. The byte count checks out: 16 x ~80K tokens x (128 B K + 128 B V) = ~328 MB, 2.1 TB/s at 156 us. reference.generate_input builds the page table from a torch.randperm over batch*max_pages, so every token's K row and V row is an independent random 128-byte line spread over ~350 MB. The kernel design itself is reasonable for H200. Kernel A has 264 persistent CTAs with 64 KB of cp.async ring each, ~128 KB in flight per SM; Little's law needs only ~20 KB/SM to sustain 3.3 TB/s at ~800 ns latency, so in-flight depth is ample. The page-index preload removes the dependent load, and 1024-token chunks over a flat (b, chunk) list balance the ragged lengths (~1280 items at decode_16 = 4.85 waves, ~97% balanced). Compute is small: mma.sync with 8 of 16 rows wasted is still far below the tensor-core roof. The fp8->f16 conversion of all 328 M K+V elements is ~164 M cvt.e4m3x2 instructions. At ~16/clk/SM that is ~40 us of ALU, which must overlap the memory stream, so it is not free at a 100 us target. Weakest link: whether FA3's 2.1 TB/s is limited by latency and in-flight depth (which this design fixes) or by HBM efficiency on uniformly random 128-byte lines plus TLB reach over a ~350 MB randomly scattered cache (which no kernel fixes). FA3 sm90 already pipelines its paged K/V loads, so the claim that FA3 'keeps the page-table load on the critical path of every tile' is unverified. Both earlier Triton gather kernels topped out at 1.6 TB/s, so there is no in-repo evidence of anything above 2.1 TB/s on this access pattern. The M1/M2 bandwidth readout (sum(cache_seqlens)*256 B / A time) is the right test. The per-load arithmetic is overstated. At the stated shape targets (105 us and 200 us), decode_16 goes from 952+2509=3461 to 952+1680=2632 (1.315x, not ~1.4x), and decode_32 from 1145+4776=5921 to 1145+3200=4345 (1.363x, not ~1.45x). That would still be ~1.10x on the 6-load geomean, about 1.42x headline. Directions are all consistent with TASK.md: decode_1, verify and sliding are outside the gate and byte-identical, so flat.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / -ab-tune-batch-gate: these build the incumbent this rewrite replaces on the gated shapes (paired FA3 plus _paired_norm_gate_kernel). They do not confound: the new kernel keeps the same one-128-byte-K-row-per-token gather, so the measured delta is purely replacing paired FA3 with kernels A and B. One implementation hazard: the paired predicate must become (window==0 and hkv%2==0 and batch>1 and not gated). Otherwise the pre-attention kernel writes the padded [T,16,128] q and kernel A reads it as [T,16,64]. Full verify_16/32 must stay paired.

fused-preattention-triton: the gated path reuses _pre_attention_kernel unchanged with PAIRED=False, the same launch master uses on unpaired paths. It is a constant ~1.3-2 us with no interaction, except that the unpaired q write is slightly smaller than the paired one, a sub-0.5 us effect.
sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: disjoint (sliding batch-1 only). No shared launches or memory, and cold L2 on every replay removes cache interaction.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is kind: rewrite, judged on kernels A+B's own profile time against the 156.8/298.5 us incumbent and the 63.2/126.4 us floors. Those times are directly readable from top_kernels, because load_inline kernels appear under their own names. Reverting pairing (ab-revert) would only compare against a slower unpaired FA3, which answers nothing new. A control that splits off the index preload or the chunk balancing would need a second full CUDA implementation; that is stage-2 tuning (C, stage count, CTAs/SM), not a disambiguator. With only 2 attention checks left today, spend one on this stage and keep one for the stage-2 fix.
rules_flags: load_inline is explicitly allowed (technical rules: 'To write native CUDA, compile it inside the file with PyTorch's load_inline'), and compile time counts toward the 15-minute run limit, not the score. A typical load_inline with torch/extension.h takes 40-90 s. Use one translation unit, functions= bindings and no extra headers, and include it in the time budget.

Compile timing: muse_attention_decode has no prepare(). 'Compiled on the first eager call, never during capture' relies on the harness calling each shape eagerly before capture, in every process it uses. Compiling at module import (or on first call with a hard torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing() guard that raises clearly) is safer. Building the kernel binary does no work on inputs, so compiling at import is not 'work outside the timed call'. Verify that the image has nvcc and ninja, or the run fails at the first gated test.

Grid and workspace come from shapes and config only, with no .item() and device-pointer scales: OK. Data-dependent loop bounds inside the kernel (chunk prefix sums from cache_seqlens) are fine under graph capture. The per-call torch.empty workspace (~5-11 MB) is a graph-pool allocation sized from page_table.shape: OK.

Every key: chunks cover [0, cache_seqlens[b]) completely, and only tokens >= cache_seqlens are masked. There is no skipping by weight. The new token's key is stored by _pre_attention_kernel on the same stream before kernel A: OK.
Precision: q stays FP8 E4M3 (up-converted exactly to f16), K/V stay FP8 and are widened to f16 in registers, P is f16 (finer than FA3's fp8 P), accumulation is fp32. All within the rules.

Gate robustness (not a rule break, but final review reruns nearby shapes): the spec assumes B<=64 in shared memory and exactly 2*132 CTAs. Add batch <= 64 to the gate, and take the SM count from torch.cuda.get_device_properties rather than hard-coding 132.
open_questions: Is FA3's 2.1 TB/s latency-bound or limited by DRAM efficiency on random rows? If kernel A also stalls near 2.0-2.5 TB/s with a deep ring and balanced chunks, random 128-byte HBM3e efficiency plus TLB reach over the ~350 MB randomly permuted cache is the ceiling, and the rewrite should stop. Report achieved bandwidth and, if the profile allows, sector and L2-miss ratios.

Conversion cost: should QK use the native FP8 mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 path (sm_89+), with q already FP8, so K needs no cvt? That roughly halves conversion ALU. V still needs widening, or an FP8 P@V with P rounded to e4m3 as FA3 does.

Only one test exercises the gated path: batch 4, ctx 80000, spread mixed, coherent, page 1, with lengths up to ~4x ctx, so ~313 chunks per request and a larger workspace. kv_scale != 1 never reaches kernel A in tests. Is a local CPU or emulated check of the scale path worth adding before stage 2?

Kernel B: one warp per (request, head) serially merging ~80 partials (decode_16) to ~85 (decode_32), with C=1024, reads ~5-11 MB in total. Check that it stays at or below FA3 combine plus norm-gate (~6 us). If not, use two-level reduction or larger C in stage 2.
Losing FA3's PDL overlap between pre-attention, main and combine costs ~1-2 us per shape. Consider cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization on A and B in a later stage.
